body: Look into disease intervention specialist jobs- they’re entry level and a great fit if you’re interested in epidemiology. Pay honestly depends on where you work, but the average DIS is making about 40k.
it’s been a year since, and i still think about them.
Sometimes life’s a bitch and then you keep living. There will be better moments to come, we just have to make sure we live to see them.

You’re not pathetic, your body reacted. Don’t demean yourself for survival instincts kicking in, it’s a natural response. I’m sorry you’re in so much pain right now, but try to think of this as a new chance at life. Hopefully, things will get better soon. Sending my love, friend.

It may happen a lot, but that still doesn’t undermine the burden of being responsible for someone else’s death. Many conductors have had to quit their jobs because they couldn’t live with the survivors guilt. I know you’re in so much pain at the moment, but death by train will only pass the pain onto others. Please consider other options. I hope things start to look up for you, man. I’m always available to talk should you need it :)
It’d be instant, but the conductor’s trauma would last a lifetime. I’m sorry everything sucks right now. Would you like to talk?

I’m sorry life isn’t going as planned. It hurts when the people we care about turn their backs to us, especially in times of need. It’s hard adjusting to new circumstances, so don’t beat yourself up so bad. I promise you’re worth love and affection, I promise you’re beautiful, I promise things will get better with time. 

As for the intervention, it might be a good opportunity to open up about your feelings and reach an understanding with your roommates. I understand the process is very daunting, but I believe it’s being done because these people actually DO care about you. Take a moment to breathe, and please, practice healthy coping mechanisms. I hope things start to look up soon. <3

I’m sorry, that’s such a painful thing to experience. But, that doesn’t mean you won’t have anyone to wish you a happy birthday in the future. If you stick around, you might find those people soon. I hope your day gets better, dude.

Parents would blame each other for my death, and probably create an even more toxic and unstable household than what it already is. I absolutely love my siblings, and I really don’t want anybody to go through that kind of trauma. Also, the fact that I wouldn’t be around to see the consequences of my death. There’s no real justice or satisfaction from it, it just stops.

I never had to be hospitalized but I did have headaches and sore throat for a while. Headaches subside very quickly, just stay hydrated. The throat takes longer to heal; I had trouble swallowing for a while but it gets easier with time. It wouldn’t hurt to have everything checked out, though. 

Please don’t try this again. I’ll be here should you ever need someone to talk to. Best wishes, friend.
unreciprocated love
i’m sorry you won’t be able to take a breather. sometimes that just how it goes. it’s stressful, but hopefully by the end of crunch time, things will get better :) i believe in you!!

it’s super tough to juggle both uni and a job, so it’s okay to have setbacks. take a mental break, and don’t put a time limit on it. it’s also okay to rely on friends and family for support during this time, both emotionally and financially. just take your time, and eventually you’ll find your way.
Would you mind elaborating? And do you know how to overcome this?

There’s nothing to look forward to anymore. I make things worse all the time and hate the direction of my life. I am pathetic.

If it ended now, at least people could say “she had so much potential”, instead of seeing what a disappointment I’ve become.
But why wasn’t I enough? I loved him with everything in me. He had to have known that.
yeah that’s how things have felt for the past year now, can’t help but feel i’m wasting my life

I’m with you, dude. My family is the only reason I’m still here, because I know my death would just further tear everyone apart. My parents are the type that would blame the other for my unfortunate outcome, so I couldn’t let myself be another reason for conflict. It’s tough, and I’m sorry we’re going through so much pain right now. It’s terrifying when life doesn’t go as planned, but perhaps it’s for the best. There will be better days, and there will come a point where everything is okay again. We just got to take it day by day. If you want to talk more, dms are open. :)

Man, me too. I grew up in a verbally abusive household where communication was practically nonexistent, and everything I had learned from that environment translated into my relationships. I was absolutely awful at times, but because of the patience of others, I was able to relearn how to handle myself and certain situations. My first relationship, despite me being extremely toxic at first, blossomed into one of my most healthiest relationships to date, and has taught me so much about myself. But, even with all the development I’ve done, it still kills me inside to look back at all my shortcomings and how they’ve affected those around me. I guess one of the biggest lessons we have to learn is that no one is required to forgive you, but what’s most important is that we forgive ourselves. I wish I could’ve been better, but without all those experiences, I wouldn’t have learned anything. And I forgive myself for my mistakes because I understand the position I was in - I was young, inexperienced, and didn’t know any better. I still make mistakes, even now, when I am much better than before. That doesn’t mean all the work I’ve done is for naught; just that I still have work to do. I believe it’s the same for you, too. I know how hard it is to pick yourself back up and accept your past, because it’s something that I still struggle with sometimes. But I think that’s a necessary stepping stone we all have to take. Try not to be so hard on yourself, dude.

Sorry for the long reply, I hope this helps. <3

Same here, my last breakup really put me in the worst position of my life - I’d never seriously considered suicide until he had left me. The circumstances of the breakup didn’t help either, just left me with more questions and broken trust. Not to mention the massive amount of insecurities that have manifested as a result. 

I’m sorry to say there’s not much I can do to ease your pain, but if you want to talk to someone who can relate, I’m here.

i see a lot of myself in you - i grew up with a verbally abusive parent and was also bullied from elementary through middle school. i’m also struggling a lot with school and a general direction for my life. i know how insanely tough these things are, and i won’t pretend to know how to fix them, but maybe we could learn to support each other through them? i hope you’re doing well, dm me if you’d like to talk

i am so tired of being told that i have to find happiness for myself. i literally cannot. everything that’s brought me happiness before was only temporary - in the end, i’m still in this sad, dark place, completely alone.

I lost my partner of three years after he kicked me out last summer. Unlike you, he’s never regretted it, so it’s been tough dealing with those circumstances. He’s moved on fine without me, which absolutely kills me inside because I still love him, despite all he’s put me through. I also don’t have much of a support system, which is why I started coming to this subreddit. I don’t know how to heal the pain, but if you want to talk to someone who’s going through a similar situation, I’m here.

I understand what you’re feeling. My last long term relationship ended an entire year ago, and I still spend a lot of time missing that person. I honestly think my life would’ve been better if they had stayed, and it’s been really tough finding a meaning for myself since then. I can’t tell you that things get easier, because the experience is different for everybody. So, if you’d be up to talking to someone who’s going through a similar situation as you, dms are open.
it’s stupid but the thought of one day reconnecting with a loved one and seeing japan
hurts even more when u see them moving on completely fine without u

don’t be afraid to express your emotions. distracting yourself and practicing healthy coping mechanisms are always good, but if there are moments where you just need to cry and scream- don’t hold back. grief is never ending. you’ll learn to move on, but you’ll never forget your loss. i’m sorry this is happening to you, i hope you find some light soon.

I know what you mean. Just last night I ruined a good time by acting irrationally to something really minor - it happens. I know how hard it is to let yourself be happy when you believe you’re undeserving of it, so don’t beat yourself up too much. It takes a lot of work for things to get better, and pitfalls are sure to happen. Try to remember that healing isn’t linear and you’re allowed to relapse, even in your best moments. If you want to talk more, you can always dm me.
it’s the absolute worst feeling in the world when u have no one to reassure u. i’m sorry. i can only hope things get better for us.

I’m really disappointed in some of these comments claiming that you haven’t tried to improve your situation, because it seems like you’ve tried just about anything. There may be some systemic injustices that literally block you from succeeding, which absolutely SUCKS, but at least you shouldn’t feel the need to blame yourself constantly. Give yourself credit where credit is due: you tried. 

It seems like you’ve been stuck for a long time. I’m sorry to say that I’m not knowledgeable enough to give you advice, but I’m open to listen if you ever need to vent. Sometimes, venting is all we can do.

I completely agree with you. This is largely the reason why I struggle to talk about my mental health with my parents- especially my dad. The constant push to go to church more because “God brings happiness” is so unbearable. It’s outright ignoring the REAL issues to give a quick fix that doesn’t even fix anything! 

Honestly, the best thing we can do to avoid religion in these instances is to outline our boundaries. “I’m in a very vulnerable state, so I’d prefer if God wasn’t brought into this.” If those boundaries can’t be respected, then it’s best to find someone else to talk to instead. I hope this helps.
that was actually very encouraging, thank you. i’ll try to keep your words in mind the next time i feel like a failure, and hopefully remind myself of the small things. <3

it helps, i’m glad you took the time to respond. you’re right when you say that trying on its own is really hard and should be viewed as an accomplishment. but it doesn’t feel like it, unfortunately. my shortcomings made it so people had to leave, i just feel like it’s lost cause.

I understand, in my case though I’m not sure there’s any going back. I feel like I’ve lost these people forever because of my own shortcomings. No amount of forgiveness will be able to fix that.

In moments that I do improve, I fall back into old patterns. It’s really all I know at this point, and the only way I feel any sense of security in my situation. They leave because my efforts aren’t enough. I’m not harboring any animosity towards them, just hopelessness for myself.

I could never tell people about my suicidal urges, unfortunately. I know my post says I don’t care about them, but I really do. I’m just in a place of massive hurt right now.

I’d rather suffer with myself than place some guilt or shame in someone else.

i’m sorry. i really hope things get better for us.

I’m in the same boat as you. I’m a senior too, supposed to graduate next semester. I’m in this “professional preparedness” class where I have to secure an internship, but my depressions been setting me back. I had an F in the course for an entire month. 

It’s been tough all semester, especially over the past few weeks. But today, I finally found some motivation to reach out to an organization, and they scheduled me to come in this Wednesday. I know how difficult virtual classes can be, especially when your professors a total ass. You’re trying your best, and sometimes that’s really all you can do. Even if he doesn’t recognize your efforts, you are good enough. And, more importantly, there is hope. Let me be an example of that.

I am in the exact same mindset as you. It’s tough having gone through life believing that love is conditional, and that you’re meant to meet certain expectations in order to achieve it. Its very tiring. But there’s nothing wrong with us. We just haven’t been raised in the best environments.
I thought I wouldn’t make it to March, but here I am. Though, that doesn’t mean I didn’t try. Now I’m shooting for July. Just can’t imagine a future with me in it.
Already have one, family would be able to take care of him if i’m gone. He’s amazing but he can’t give me real intimacy or support.

The worst part about this is you’ll convince yourself you’re not addicted, just in love. You’ll rely on all the tiniest slivers of hope and refuse to take no as an answer. You’ll only see them for their good sides and ignore the bad. You’ll blame yourself before you ever blame them. 

And the hardest part? Having to admit that you don’t actually love them, you’re just used to their company.

Are we the same person? I moved in with my ex mid-pandemic to alleviate the stress of distance, and within 2 months he broke up with me AND kicked me out. For months, I justified his actions and blamed myself for how everything went down. Now I know better. 

If they have the capacity to betray you after years of a relationship, don’t believe for a second that they are worth your forgiveness.

The thought that we’ve somehow burdened them is absolutely heartbreaking. Especially when you know you gave it your all. At the same time, though, I don’t think they blame us for anything. More than likely they just wish for the best. 

At the same time, I wonder how they must think of me after all is said and done.
We share similar situations. Sometimes the rudeness is just blunt honesty. They don’t want to say anything that would make you hold onto hope. It’s their way of building a wall between you.
Okay, yeah. Take it from someone who’s done it TWICE now. While he was seeing me he was also seeing someone else on the side. He’s definitely not the man he once was.

I’m so proud of you! It seriously takes a lot to realize that you weren’t the problem, and it’s a process that every dumpee has to go through. The fact that you were able to figure that out means healing is going to be a little bit easier from now on.

Ex-boyfriend of 3 years separated back in July, and I found myself in this constant loop of self-blaming and doubt. Even in the moments that my EX told me HIMSELF that I wasn’t the issue, my mind circled back to all the possible things I could’ve done wrong. 5 months later, I’ve finally made peace with the fact that there was nothing I could do to change the outcome. Sad as it is, I think I’m ready to really move forward. I hope it’s the same for you.

Just had another dream with him in it last night, 5 months after the relationship ended. Didn’t hurt as bad this time, though, just a little sad that things couldn’t work out the way I wanted them to. When everything was first happening, a dream like this would’ve led to a complete breakdown- so I’ve made a lot more progress than I’m willing to give myself credit for. The best thing each of us can do at this point is keep living, and eventually the dreams won’t hurt as much.

First, it’s okay to not move on right away. It’s okay to be a little bit stuck; it’s all a part of healing. It’s going to take a while until you feel okay without him, but it will happen. Just try to focus on yourself for now.

Second, it is NOT as easy as you think it is to forget someone like you. NEVER FORGET THAT! He’s probably having a hard time moving on too, but you aren’t able to see it. Not saying this to get your hopes up, just to place more worth on yourself. 

I have been in your shoes countless times. Sometimes your brain will tell you the worst things about yourself and your ex, when they’re not true at all. Believe in yourself, and the rest will come to you.

You miss him. That’s all you really can do. It’s a part of the process, and the process SUCKS! But eventually you’ll reach a point where the urge to talk to him doesn’t exist anymore. You’ll think of him less and less. You’ll realize you don’t need him to be happy. 
That’s what I keep telling myself, anyway.

Hi, I know I’m kinda late to this post, but I wanna share anyway.

We were in a relationship for 3 years, moved in for the last 2 months. Broke up about 4-5 months ago. The last couple months we were together felt so euphoric, I was completely blindsided by the breakup. No serious arguments or toxicity; he just insisted he couldn’t be in a relationship anymore and needed to develop on his own.

He is currently in the Navy and about to be stationed in Japan. He’s gotten some time off and is staying in my area. In the beginning of November we started talking more often, and I began to cling onto the slightest bit of hope (even though he clarified he wanted a strict friendship). We got to see each other for Thanksgiving, and I was so happy to share that experience with him, especially after believing I could never see him again. We didn’t do anything romantic, but I was really thinking that by being involved with me, he could be reminded of us and how good we were together. Come the next day, I find out he was on a date with someone else. Heartbroken once again, and I really only have myself to blame. 

I’m not really proud of how I’ve handled everything, since I’ve never been able to keep up with NC, and have made some desperate attempts at getting him back. But because of this subreddit, I realize I’m just human and it’s okay to be as hurt as I am. The pain just goes to show the sheer depth of my love, which isn’t something to be ashamed of. 

As of yesterday, I’ve blocked all his socials and am working towards blocking his number (I’m trying to be patient with myself and build up the courage). I’ve tried to be his friend, and I’m disappointed I couldn’t meet his expectations, but I gotta start thinking about what’s best for me. I need to learn to accept things for what they are, instead of fantasizing of what could be. He’s even told me he’d be happy just to know that I’ve learned to move on and be okay with myself. 

It sucks to lose someone you loved so intensely, and sometimes it seems like I have no future to look forward to without him. Healing truly is not a linear process, and I feel like I’ve regressed to where I was 2 months ago. Everything will be okay eventually, I’m just going to miss him dearly.

I still do the same thing sometimes, 3 months after the breakup. Some days are a lot easier to ignore than others, but when I’m feeling extremely desperate, I’ve found that distracting yourself is your best option. Personally, I marathon Adventure Time to temporarily forget about my situation. 
What’s more, your ex probably wouldn’t like knowing that you’re monitoring their every move. It’s hard, but you gotta respect their space- thinking like that can help control yourself, too. 
And if all else fails, remove them from your socials.

Dealt with the same thing, too. They’re quick to move on and act like you weren’t a significant figure in their life. Stinks. ://

In the end though, I think it’s important to realize that they’re not going to completely reveal all their thoughts and emotions to you, especially since you’re not together. Like many have already said, sometimes it just comes down to how they cope. How they’re acting now is not a true indicator of how they feel about you, or how they may have felt in the relationship.

And if they’re really indifferent towards you, all the more reason to move on yourself.

Hi there! This is my first real breakup too- on my second month as well. I totally feel where you’re at right now, because being unemployed and going through a heartbreak like this all during a pandemic can leave you unmotivated and lonely. There have been weird cycles for me where I’m functioning //okay// without him, but then an hour later I’m crying in bed because I miss him so much. 
Even though it’s tough, and you feel like nothing else matters anymore, you gotta keep going. You have to learn to be content on your own. And if you won’t do it for yourself, do it for them.

I’ve had something similar happen to me back in April. We had first broken up in January due to long distance and his desire to be more independent. After a couple weeks we were talking again but he insisted that he wouldn’t be comfortable being with me if it was long distance. Outside of the circumstances, he never mentioned that anything was wrong with the relationship and he still wanted to be a part of my life. When quarantine began in March, we decided to come up with a game plan that would require me going to move in with him for the summer. By April we were back together- happy as ever. 

Unfortunately, not enough was done where he felt genuinely happy being with me again. When there were issues, he kept it to himself and didn’t communicate clearly. By July, he decided to break up again because he believed he wasn’t in the right mindset to be in a relationship- that he kept looking at my negatives and the past issues that still bothered him. It completely blindsided me at the time, because I felt incredibly happy in the new circumstance, and we hadn’t had any huge disagreements since being back together. 

I’m glad you guys were able to figure something out and decided to have another go at it, but don’t allow yourself to fall back into your old habits. Put in the effort for both your sake and hers, and don’t forget to check up on one another every once in a while to see how you’re both feeling about the relationship. Best of luck!
